events.h: eThekwini’s first council sitting ends without a mayor as the ANC and MK are reported to have a deal
events.dek: eThekwini’s inaugural council meeting adjourned on 24 November without electing a mayor, deputy mayor or speaker, to give parties time to finish coalition deals. IOL and Briefly News report the ANC and MK have reached an eThekwini agreement, though the parties were coy at the sitting.
brief: Several outlets report the council adjourned without filling a single leadership position, to allow coalition talks to conclude; IOL reports committees will be established at a 10 December meeting.
eNCA reports the sitting went ahead despite a KwaZulu-Natal Cogta directive to delay it, and DailyNews and the Sunday Tribune report the city manager challenged the directive.
IOL reports the ANC and MK sealed an eThekwini deal, and Briefly News reports an agreement was reportedly reached; EWN reports the parties were coy at the sitting.
The Sowetan reports the ANC NEC weighed competing KwaZulu-Natal proposals with an eye on Durban; IOL quotes the ANC’s Nyawose saying voters gave no party a mandate to govern alone.
The MK Party says its mayoral candidate has an “unblemished record”, IOL and The Mercury report.

events.place: Buffalo City and Nelson Mandela Bay
events.h: Faku returns in Buffalo City with the EFF as a DA-led coalition signs for Nelson Mandela Bay
events.dek: Princess Faku was re-elected Buffalo City mayor, beating the UDM’s Nqabayomzi Kwankwa, and BusinessTech reports the ANC teamed up with the EFF. In Nelson Mandela Bay, a DA-led multiparty coalition has been formed, but News24 reports an ANC-led filibuster blocked the vote for mayor and speaker.
brief: eNCA, EWN and Briefly News report Faku was re-elected; Briefly News says she defeated the UDM’s Nqabayomzi Kwankwa, and BusinessTech says the ANC is running the metro with the EFF.
News24 reports ANC divisions over Faku’s return, quoting one voice saying “you cannot smuggle her back”.

News24 says the DA will govern Nelson Mandela Bay with the FF Plus, UDM, ActionSA and PAC; several outlets report a six-party deal, SABC News reports a four-party DA-led coalition, and HeraldLIVE says Retief Odendaal is set to be mayor.

News24 reports the DA’s plan to elect a mayor and speaker was blocked by an ANC-led filibuster, The National reports there is no mayor yet, and Daily Maverick says the ANC scrambled for a last-minute coalition.
HeraldLIVE reports a 'black caucus' insists the Nelson Mandela Bay coalition is not a done deal.

events.dek: EFF leader Julius Malema went to court to stop DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille repeating claims about him, in a dispute linked to the Johannesburg coalition fight, and IOL reports he threatened R1m defamation action. Zille refused to retract, and the court reserved judgment.

News24 reports Zille fought the gag bid using Malema’s own words, including 'we were controlling him'.
IOL reports the court reserved judgment on the bid, which concerns claims of city power capture.

events.h: The DA is shut out of Theewaterskloof and Laingsburg as Western Cape councils pick partners
events.dek: News24 reports the ANC joined other parties to take control of Theewaterskloof, and IOL reports ActionSA formed a Laingsburg coalition with the PA and ANC, leaving the DA out. News24 reports the DA and FF Plus have entered coalitions in some hung Western Cape councils.
brief: News24 reports the ANC and other parties took control of Theewaterskloof, shutting out the DA; the Cape Argus reports the DA warning this could threaten financial recovery.
IOL reports ActionSA formed a coalition with the PA and ANC in Laingsburg, leaving the DA out.
News24 reports the DA and FF Plus entered coalitions in some hung councils; IOL reported the DA began talks with 16 councils hung.
IOL reports the DA named deputy mayor and speaker candidates for seven Western Cape municipalities, and Limberg as Cape Town deputy mayor.
IOL and the Weekend Argus carry an argument that the opposition’s voice in Cape Town is growing smaller and meeker.

events.h: The ANC leaves coalition choices to its provinces and regions
events.dek: EWN and Dan Corder report the ANC’s NEC has let provinces and regions decide coalitions, with consequences for Gauteng, eThekwini, Nelson Mandela Bay and over 100 hung councils. The ANC says there is consensus as talks move towards conclusion, while TimesLIVE and IOL report strains over Ramaphosa’s leadership.
brief: EWN asks whether the ANC has given provinces and regions the final say; Dan Corder says the NEC decided to let regional bodies choose, affecting well over 100 hung councils.
Newsnote reports the ANC asserting there is consensus as talks near conclusion; The Witness reports the NEC weighing up its coalition future.

Business Day reports the ANC is seeking a foothold in hung councils, EWN quotes an analyst saying its choices could decide whether it enters a 'death spiral', and IOL reports the SACP drawing a line over coalition support for the ANC.
On Gabriel Makin’s channel, Marius Roodt argues the ANC has become a federal party, noting the Gauteng ANC wants to work with MK and the EFF while Limpopo’s prefers the DA.

TimesLIVE reports Ramaphosa faces a tough ANC unity test, IOL reports tensions over Ramaphosa, election losses and working with the DA, and The Common Sense argues ANC indecision has left a power vacuum.
